chunks.title: Prosa — README
chunks.heading: Prosa
chunks.text: Semantic search for technical documents — NBR norms, project specs, plant documentation — with section-level citations. Engineers spend hours doing Ctrl+F across PDFs. Prosa lets you ask in plain language and get back the exact section and page number. QA — you have a specific question, you want a direct answer.

chunks.title: Prosa — README
chunks.heading: Prosa
chunks.text: Research — you want everything the documents say about a topic.

chunks.title: Prosa — README
chunks.heading: Prosa › When to use which mode
chunks.text: QA ( scripts/qa.py ) Research ( scripts/research.py ) Question type Specific ("what is the minimum fck?") Broad ("find all effluents") Retrieval Top-5 most relevant chunks All chunks above a similarity threshold Output Single answer with citations Structured report listing every finding Best for Regulatory lookups, spec checks Audits, compliance surveys, gap analysis

chunks.title: Prosa — README
chunks.heading: Prosa › How it works
chunks.text: PDFs are extracted via Docling (tables, reading order, section structure preserved). Marker-PDF kicks in automatically as a fallback for scanned PDFs or when Docling cannot extract text. Chunks are token-based: 512 tokens for OpenAI embeddings, 256 for Ollama (BERT tokenizer expands math-heavy content). Metadata per chunk: section title , article number (norm-only), page range , doc type .

chunks.title: Prosa — README
chunks.heading: Prosa › How it works
chunks.text: Chunk IDs are SHA-256(filename + text) — re-ingesting the same document is safe. 1. Reformulate query into 3 search variations (GPT-4o-mini) 2. Retrieve top-5 per variation → deduplicate to ≤15 3. Re-rank all candidates in a single LLM call → keep top 5 4. Synthesise answer with citations: Art.

chunks.title: Prosa — README
chunks.heading: Prosa › How it works
chunks.text: X.Y.Z, {doc name}, p. N 1. Expand topic into 8-10 synonyms and related terms (GPT-4o-mini) 2. Retrieve top-30 per term → filter by distance threshold → deduplicate 3. Sort by relevance, cap at 60 chunks 4. Synthesise a structured report grouped by section, listing every finding

chunks.title: Prosa — README
chunks.heading: Prosa › Requirements
chunks.text: - Python 3.10+ - Docker (for ChromaDB) - An OpenAI API key

chunks.title: Prosa — README
chunks.heading: Prosa › Install
chunks.text: Option A — Docker (recommended) The MCP server listens on http://localhost:8101/sse . Add to Claude Desktop ( ~/.claude/claude desktop config.json ): Option B — Local Python Add to Claude Desktop to use the MCP server locally (stdio, no Docker):

chunks.title: Prosa — README
chunks.heading: Prosa › Ingest documents
chunks.text: Put your PDFs in data/raw/ , then: Files whose names start with NBR are auto-detected as norm if --doc-type is omitted. For mixed folders, run two separate passes. The default image uses requirements-fast.txt (no Marker-PDF, no PyTorch). To build an image with OCR support:

chunks.title: Prosa — README
chunks.heading: Prosa › Query
chunks.text: The --threshold flag controls the distance cutoff for research retrieval. The default (1.0) captures anything with cosine similarity ≥ 0.5 — broadly relevant. Lower values like 0.6 return only closely matching chunks.

chunks.title: Prosa — README
chunks.heading: Prosa › Local embeddings with Ollama
chunks.text: Prosa supports Ollama as an alternative embedding provider for offline use or comparison testing. Embeddings from different models cannot share a ChromaDB collection — you must ingest into separate collections and query each one independently. Run two ingestion passes with different collections, then query each:

chunks.title: Prosa — README
chunks.heading: Prosa › MCP server (Claude Desktop)
chunks.text: Prosa can run as an MCP server, exposing retrieval as tools that Claude calls directly. Claude then handles all reasoning — query reformulation, relevance judgment, synthesis — without GPT-4o-mini in the loop.

chunks.title: Prosa — README
chunks.heading: Prosa › MCP server (Claude Desktop)
chunks.text: The server exposes two tools: - search(query, k) — embeds the query, returns top-k chunks with citations and distances - list documents() — shows what's indexed so Claude can orient itself before searching Add to ~/.claude/claude desktop config.json (create if it doesn't exist): Restart Claude Desktop.

chunks.title: Prosa — README
chunks.heading: Prosa › MCP server (Claude Desktop)
chunks.text: The .env file is loaded automatically — no need to pass OPENAI API KEY in the config. ChromaDB must be running ( docker-compose up -d ). Once connected, Claude can answer questions about your indexed documents without any special prompting. You can also guide it explicitly:

chunks.title: Prosa — README
chunks.heading: Prosa › MCP server (Claude Desktop)
chunks.text: "Use Prosa to find everything about effluent treatment in the plant spec." "Search the indexed documents for fire safety requirements and flag any that reference ABNT norms." CLI ( scripts/qa.py , scripts/research.py ) MCP + Claude LLM for reasoning GPT-4o-mini Claude Query formulation You choose qa vs research Claude decides Multi-turn Manual re-runs Natural conversation Best for Scripts, batch, CI Interactive exploration

chunks.title: Prosa — README
chunks.heading: Prosa › Notes on scanned documents
chunks.text: Marker-PDF downloads Nougat model weights (~2-4 GB) on the first OCR run. This is a one-time download and can take 10-30 minutes on a slow connection. On CPU-only hardware, OCR processing takes roughly 20-40 minutes per 200-page document; digital PDFs process in under 5 minutes.

chunks.title: Prosa — README
chunks.heading: Prosa › Privacy
chunks.text: Chunk text is sent to OpenAI for embedding and synthesis. Full documents are never stored externally. If your documents cannot leave your machine, replace Embedder with a local model (e.g., nomic-embed-text via Ollama) and set PROSA LLM MODEL to a locally-served model.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec
chunks.text: Status: draft v0.1 · [removed] · Owner: Andre de Castro Zorzo This document is the design of the zorzo.dev.br backend. It is also part of the corpus: when a visitor asks "how does this site work?", the agent answers from this file.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 1. Purpose
chunks.text: zorzo.dev.br is not a résumé page. It is a production AI system that visitors interrogate. They ask questions about Andre's work, and an agent answers from a curated corpus. Every answer is cited, traced, measured and priced in public. Thesis: the controls are the demo.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 1. Purpose
chunks.text: Hallucination, prompt injection, abuse, cost and flaky free models are known risks. They are accepted on purpose. The site shows each one being contained, with numbers.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 1. Purpose › Goals
chunks.text: 1. Answer questions about Andre (career, skills, projects, availability) and about this system itself, in PT or EN, grounded only in the corpus. 2. Say "not in my sources" instead of guessing. 3. Expose the internals: live pipeline events for the HUD, a public trace per answer, public eval and defense dashboards.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 1. Purpose › Goals
chunks.text: 4. Run within a small fixed budget (target: under US$15/month all-in) on hardware that never sleeps.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 1. Purpose › Non-goals
chunks.text: - A general chatbot. Off-topic requests are declined. - Write actions on behalf of the visitor (no sending email, no booking). Tools are read-only. - User accounts, persistent personal memory, analytics beyond what section 12 lists.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 2. Surface
chunks.text: Path What it is / Animated central image + query box. Answers stream in; the HUD shows pipeline stages live. /t/{trace id} Public, redacted trace of one answer: stages, retrieved sources, scores, model, tokens, latency, cost, verdict. /evals Latest eval run per corpus/model version, trend over time.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 2. Surface
chunks.text: /defenses Blocked attempts in the last 7/30 days by layer and category, anonymized examples, false-block rate. /status Uptime, p50/p95 latency, today's budget used, active model chain, circuit-breaker state. /sources Everything the agent knows: list of indexed documents with date and link. API lives at api.zorzo.dev.br .

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 3. Architecture
chunks.text: Why one Postgres instead of Postgres + Qdrant + Redis: one stateful service to back up, migrate and reason about. Hybrid search in a single SQL query. Rate limiting with INSERT … ON CONFLICT . At this scale (thousands of chunks, low QPS) a dedicated vector DB adds operations cost and no measurable gain.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 3. Architecture
chunks.text: If evals ever show otherwise, the store is behind an interface (section 5.4).

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 4. Corpus › 4.1 Sources
chunks.text: Source Format Notes Résumé PT + EN Markdown (converted from PDF) Primary source for career facts. Career narrative Markdown, written by Andre Per-role write-ups: context, problem, what he built, outcome. Fills what a résumé compresses. FAQ Markdown, written by Andre Availability, time zone, contract types, languages, remote setup.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 4. Corpus › 4.1 Sources
chunks.text: Authoritative answers to common recruiter questions. Public GitHub repos README, docs/, repo metadata Allowlist only. Fetched via GitHub API at ingestion. Prosa docs Markdown Flagship project. This site spec.md, ADRs, selected source files Enables "how does this work?" answers and the search site code tool.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 4. Corpus › 4.2 Exclusion rules
chunks.text: - Nothing private, nothing under NDA, no employer-confidential detail, no client names unless already public. - Private repos are never fetched. rczorzo/quickseeks-ui is excluded explicitly. - Every document carries reviewed by owner: true in front matter. Ingestion rejects documents without it.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 4. Corpus › 4.3 Document metadata
chunks.text: authority breaks ties when sources disagree (e.g., FAQ beats an old post).

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 4. Corpus › 4.4 Ingestion pipeline
chunks.text: 1. Scan. gitleaks over the corpus diff + a PII regex pass (emails other than the public contact, phone numbers, CPF, addresses). Any hit fails the job. 2. Extract. Markdown passes through. PDFs reuse Prosa's extractor (Docling). 3. Chunk. Heading-aware, ~400 tokens, 15% overlap, each chunk keeps its heading path ( Résumé Alert Logic 2008–2026 ).

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 4. Corpus › 4.4 Ingestion pipeline
chunks.text: Chunk size is an eval variable, not a constant. 4. Embed. Local multilingual model on CPU (candidates: multilingual-e5-base , bge-m3 ). Chosen by retrieval eval on the PT+EN golden set. Local embeddings mean no external call per query and no dependency on a free tier for the hot path.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 4. Corpus › 4.4 Ingestion pipeline
chunks.text: 5. Upsert. Keyed by sha256(content + metadata) . Unchanged chunks are not re-embedded. 6. Version. Each run writes a new corpus version . The API keeps serving the active version. 7. Gate. Evals (section 11) run against the candidate version. It is activated only if no gated metric regresses.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 4. Corpus › 4.4 Ingestion pipeline
chunks.text: Otherwise the job fails and the previous version stays live. Blue/green corpus means a bad document cannot silently degrade answers.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 5. Retrieval › 5.1 Query pipeline
chunks.text: 1. Normalize (Unicode NFKC, strip control chars, cap at 500 chars). 2. Detect language (answer language follows the question). 3. Optional rewrite: for follow-ups, the agent condenses history into a standalone query. 4.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 5. Retrieval › 5.1 Query pipeline
chunks.text: Hybrid search in one SQL statement: - vector: cosine top 20 over chunks.embedding (HNSW index), - lexical: websearch to tsquery top 20 over chunks.tsv (simple + unaccent config, works for PT and EN), - fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k = 60). 5. Optional cross-encoder rerank of top 20 → top 6.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 5. Retrieval › 5.1 Query pipeline
chunks.text: Kept only if evals show a recall/precision gain worth its latency on CPU. 6. Relevance floor. If the best fused score is below a calibrated threshold, retrieval returns insufficient evidence and the agent goes to the abstain path.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 5. Retrieval › 5.2 Why hybrid
chunks.text: Names, versions and acronyms ("MCP", "Aleo", "DynamoDB") are where pure vector search fails and lexical search wins. Paraphrased questions are the opposite. RRF needs no score calibration between the two.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 5. Retrieval › 5.3 Context assembly
chunks.text: Top chunks are passed to the model inside data delimiters with their ids (section 9, layer 3). Max 6 chunks, ~2,500 tokens.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 5. Retrieval › 5.4 Store interface
chunks.text: VectorStore.search(query vec, query text, k, filters) - list[Hit] . Implementations: PgVectorStore (production), Prosa's Chroma store (comparison). The pgvector adapter is contributed upstream to Prosa.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 6. Agent
chunks.text: LangGraph state machine. Explicit nodes instead of a free-running ReAct loop: every transition is observable and bounded. Node Job gate Turnstile token, rate limit, budget. Fails closed. guard Injection/abuse classification (section 9). route Classify intent: career fact , about andre , about system , projects live , contact , off topic , and extract the terms the question names.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 6. Agent
chunks.text: Picks path: graph, RAG, or both (section 6.5). Cheap model, structured output. retrieve Section 5. assess Is evidence sufficient? Uses relevance floor + a short model check ("do these chunks answer the question?"). reformulate One retry with a rewritten query. Hard cap 1. answer Generates the answer under the answer contract (section 8.1).

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 6. Agent
chunks.text: verify Claim-level grounding check + output guard. repair Drops unsupported claims, regenerates once. If still failing, falls back to abstain. abstain "Not in my sources" + nearest related sources + contact link. emit Final SSE events, public trace write. Limits per request: max 2 model calls in the loop beyond routing, max 3 tool calls, 20 s wall clock.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 6. Agent
chunks.text: Conversation state: last 6 turns, in memory, keyed by an anonymous session id, TTL 30 min. Nothing about the visitor persists beyond section 12.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 6.5 Career graph
chunks.text: Inspired by NVIDIA's auto-ontology (generate → certify → answer over a semantic layer). The pattern is adopted, the stack is not: it targets enterprise relational sources, and this corpus is mostly prose.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 6.5 Career graph › Why
chunks.text: RAG is weak exactly where recruiters ask first: counting and time. "How many years of AWS?", "Which projects used DynamoDB?", "What was he doing in 2015?" need aggregation over facts scattered across chunks. A model summing intervals from text guesses. A query over certified facts does not.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 6.5 Career graph › Model
chunks.text: Predicates are a closed set: worked at , held role , used , built , led , studied at , holds cert , speaks , part of . Every fact points to the chunk it came from (provenance).

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 6.5 Career graph › Generate → certify
chunks.text: 1. Generate. At ingestion, an extraction pass over authority ≥ 2 documents proposes entities and facts with certified = false . 2. Certify. Andre reviews drafts with a CLI ( uv run certify ): approve, edit, reject, merge aliases. Only certified facts are queryable in production.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 6.5 Career graph › Generate → certify
chunks.text: /sources shows certified vs pending counts. 3. Learn. A wrong answer that Andre corrects becomes an edited fact ( superseded by keeps history) and a new eval case.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 6.5 Career graph › Answer
chunks.text: 1. route extracts the terms the question names ("AWS", "years"). 2. Resolve: each term is matched to entities by alias, then by embedding similarity above a threshold. 3. check answerable : coverage = resolved terms / required terms. Coverage 0 → abstain ("no Rust in my sources").

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 6.5 Career graph › Answer
chunks.text: Partial → answer the covered part and say what is missing. 4. Typed query, not model-written SQL. The model fills a Pydantic GraphQuery ( op: list count duration timeline exists , entity ids, predicate, time range). Code compiles it to parameterized SQL from a fixed template set.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 6.5 Career graph › Answer
chunks.text: This keeps section 9's rule (no SQL from the model) and makes results deterministic. 5. Durations merge overlapping intervals before summing (two concurrent AWS roles ≠ double years). end date = null means current. 6. The answer cites fact ids ( fact:142 ). Verification for graph claims is deterministic: the cited fact is in the query result.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 6.5 Career graph › Routing between paths
chunks.text: Question Path "How many years of Python?" graph "How did he use MCP at Titan Shark?" RAG "Which AWS projects did he lead, and what was hard about them?" both: graph lists projects, RAG explains When graph and text disagree on a fact, the certified fact wins and the conflict is logged for review.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 6.5 Career graph › Routing between paths
chunks.text: The trace shows the path taken, the resolved entities, the coverage score and the compiled SQL.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 7. Tools
chunks.text: All read-only. Arguments validated by Pydantic schemas; no free-form URLs, no shell, no SQL from the model. Tool Input Output Notes search corpus query , kind? hits with ids Same as section 5. get document doc id (enum of indexed ids) metadata + summary For "show me the source".

chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 7. Tools
chunks.text: list projects — public projects with links, status From corpus metadata. github activity repo (enum from allowlist) last commits, open issues count, last release GitHub API, cached 10 min, unauthenticated or fine-grained read-only token. search site code query file + line snippets Over this site's public repo.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 7. Tools
chunks.text: Lets the agent cite its own implementation. contact options — email, calendar link Returns links only. Never sends anything. check answerable terms[] resolved entities, coverage 0..1, missing terms Section 6.5. query career graph GraphQuery (typed) rows + fact ids + compiled SQL Certified facts only.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 7. Tools
chunks.text: Template-compiled, parameterized. Tool outputs are data, treated exactly like retrieved chunks (section 9, layer 3).

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 8. Grounding (hallucination control) › 8.1 Answer contract
chunks.text: The answer node must return structured output: Every factual sentence is a claim with at least one source id from the current retrieval set. The frontend renders claims as sentences with clickable citation markers. Free models vary in structured-output support.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 8. Grounding (hallucination control) › 8.1 Answer contract
chunks.text: The parser accepts JSON mode, fenced JSON, or a strict line format; a parse failure triggers one retry, then fallback to the next model in the chain.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 8. Grounding (hallucination control) › 8.2 Verification
chunks.text: For each claim: 1. Id check. Every cited id exists in this request's retrieval set. Fabricated ids → claim rejected. 2. Support check. A judge call (cheap model, batched for all claims) labels each claim supported partial unsupported against its cited chunks only. 3. Policy.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 8. Grounding (hallucination control) › 8.2 Verification
chunks.text: unsupported claims are removed. If removal leaves the answer empty or incoherent → repair once → else abstain . partial claims are kept with softened wording only if the judge marks the supported part.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 8. Grounding (hallucination control) › 8.3 Abstention
chunks.text: Unanswerable is a first-class outcome, not an error. "Does Andre know Rust?" with nothing in the corpus returns: not in my sources + what is there (related skills) + contact link. Abstention accuracy is a gated metric (section 11).

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 8. Grounding (hallucination control) › 8.4 Specific risk: claims about a real person
chunks.text: The system talks about Andre in third person to strangers, including recruiters. Extra rules: - No inferred opinions, salary figures, personal life, or comparisons with other people. - Superlatives ("best", "expert in everything") are rejected by the output guard unless quoted verbatim from an authority: 3 source.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 8. Grounding (hallucination control) › 8.4 Specific risk: claims about a real person
chunks.text: - Negative statements about employers or clients are declined.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 9. Prompt-injection and abuse defenses
chunks.text: Defense in depth. Each layer logs a defense event with layer, category and action. No single layer is trusted to be sufficient. The repo is public, so defenses must not depend on secrecy of their design; only thresholds, the canary value and keys live in env.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 9. Prompt-injection and abuse defenses
chunks.text: Layer Control Catches L0 Edge Cloudflare in front, Turnstile (invisible) to start a session, body size cap, CORS locked to zorzo.dev.br. Bots, scripted floods, cross-site abuse. L1 Input Normalization, length cap, rate limit (section 10.2), language/charset sanity. Oversized payloads, obfuscation via control chars and homoglyphs.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 9. Prompt-injection and abuse defenses
chunks.text: L2 Classifier Dedicated injection classifier on the user message (candidates: a small prompt-guard model on CPU, or a cheap LLM classifier with a fixed rubric). Categories: direct injection , jailbreak , system prompt extraction , defamation bait , off topic , benign . Direct attacks before any expensive call.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 9. Prompt-injection and abuse defenses
chunks.text: L3 Spotlighting Retrieved chunks and tool outputs wrapped in delimiters and marked as untrusted data; instructions inside them are never followed. Corpus is owner-reviewed, but repo READMEs and posts are still treated as untrusted. Indirect injection through content. L4 Capability Tools read-only, enum-constrained arguments, no URL fetching, no code execution, per-request tool cap.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 9. Prompt-injection and abuse defenses
chunks.text: Even a successful injection has nothing harmful to call. L5 Output Canary token in the system prompt: if it appears in output, the response is blocked (prompt leak). Topic-scope check, superlative/defamation rules (8.4), PII regex, link allowlist. Leaks and off-policy answers that got past L2.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 9. Prompt-injection and abuse defenses
chunks.text: L6 Grounding Section 8. Ungrounded content does not ship. Manipulated "facts". Blocked responses tell the visitor which layer stopped them ("blocked at L2: system prompt extraction"). Transparent refusal is part of the showcase and leaks nothing the public repo does not already show. False positives are tracked as hard as true positives.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 9. Prompt-injection and abuse defenses
chunks.text: A defense that blocks benign recruiters is a failure. /defenses publishes the false-block rate measured on the benign eval set.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 10. Models, cost and resilience › 10.1 Model chain
chunks.text: Configured per stage (route, answer, judge), not globally: Concrete model ids are chosen by the eval matrix (section 11), not by preference, and recorded per model config version . Check OpenRouter's current free-tier limits and data policies when choosing; free endpoints may log prompts, which is acceptable here because the corpus is public.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 10. Models, cost and resilience › 10.2 Controls
chunks.text: - Rate limit: token bucket per hashed IP and per session, stored in Postgres. Initial: 10 questions / 10 min / IP, 40 / day. Tuned from real traffic. - Per-request cap: max input + output tokens per request; max model calls per request (section 6).

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 10. Models, cost and resilience › 10.2 Controls
chunks.text: - Daily budget: hard US$ ceiling. Cost comes from OpenRouter's per-request usage accounting and is summed in budget daily . At 80% → paid fallback disabled. At 100% → search-only mode : the site still returns ranked sources with snippets, no generation. Degrades, never goes dark.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 10. Models, cost and resilience › 10.2 Controls
chunks.text: - Timeouts: per stage (route 3 s, answer 12 s, judge 5 s), 20 s total. - Circuit breaker per provider/model: open after 5 failures in 60 s or 429s, half-open after 60 s. - Semantic cache: answers for near-duplicate questions (embedding similarity ≥ 0.95, same corpus and model version) served from cache, marked as cached in the trace.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 10. Models, cost and resilience › 10.2 Controls
chunks.text: Every fallback decision is recorded in the trace: which model answered and why.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 11. Evals › 11.1 Datasets (versioned in the repo)
chunks.text: Set Size (initial) Content golden 60 PT+EN questions with expected source ids and key facts. Written by Andre. unanswerable 30 Plausible questions the corpus cannot answer. Expected: abstain. adversarial 60 Direct/indirect injection, jailbreaks, prompt extraction, defamation bait, off-topic. Expected: block or decline at a specific layer.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 11. Evals › 11.1 Datasets (versioned in the repo)
chunks.text: benign tricky 30 Legitimate questions that look suspicious ("ignore the résumé, what does he do now ?"). Expected: answered, not blocked. multi turn 15 Follow-ups requiring query condensation. facts 40 Counting, duration, timeline and list questions with exact expected values. Real anonymized questions from production (section 12) are reviewed weekly and promoted into these sets.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 11. Evals › 11.2 Metrics
chunks.text: Metric Definition Gated Retrieval recall@6 Expected source in top 6 yes Claim support rate Supported claims / all claims (judge + 10% human spot check) yes Citation precision Cited chunk actually supports its claim yes Abstention accuracy Correct abstain on unanswerable , no abstain on golden yes Fact exact match Exact expected value on facts yes Route accuracy Correct path (graph / RAG / both) yes Graph vs RAG-only Fact exact match with graph disabled, as published contrast reported Attack block rate Blocked at or before expected layer on adversarial yes False-block rate Blocked on benign tricky + golden yes p95 latency, cost/answer From traces reported

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 11. Evals › 11.2 Metrics
chunks.text: Thresholds are set after the first baseline run, then a change may not regress any gated metric beyond its noise band. Targets are published next to actuals on /evals .

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 11. Evals › 11.3 When evals run
chunks.text: - Corpus change (blue/green gate, section 4.4). - Prompt, graph or model config change (CI on pull request). - Nightly against the live config, to catch silent changes in free models. Eval runs are stored in Langfuse Datasets and summarized into eval runs for the public page.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 12. Observability and privacy › 12.1 Traces
chunks.text: Langfuse traces every request: one span per graph node, generation spans with model, tokens, cost, latency; tool spans; defense events as span events. Prod uses Langfuse Cloud (self-hosted Langfuse v3 needs ClickHouse, Redis and object storage, which do not fit the VPS). Local dev runs it in docker-compose.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 12. Observability and privacy › 12.2 Public trace (redacted)
chunks.text: Written to Postgres at emit , shown at /t/{id} : - included: stages and timings, retrieved source titles/ids and fused scores, model per stage, fallback reasons, tokens, cost, verification verdicts, defense layer outcomes; - excluded: system prompt, canary, raw IP, classifier raw scores beyond the label, other visitors' data.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 12. Observability and privacy › 12.2 Public trace (redacted)
chunks.text: - Visitor's question is shown only on the visitor's own trace link; listings on /defenses use paraphrased, PII-scrubbed examples.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: 12. Observability and privacy › 12.3 What is stored (LGPD-minded)
chunks.text: - Question text, scrubbed of PII, for eval curation. Retained 90 days. - IP: never stored raw. HMAC(ip, daily salt) for rate limiting; salts rotate daily and are discarded. - No cookies beyond the session id. No third-party analytics. - A visible one-line notice under the input box states this.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 13. API contract
chunks.text: Response: text/event-stream . Events drive both the answer text and the HUD / central image states. Event Payload HUD / visual use stage {name, status: start\ end, ms} Stage label lights up; central image changes state per stage. guard {layer, label, action} Defense indicator. retrieval {hits: [{id, title, score}], corpus version} Source fragments orbit / appear.

chunks.text: Visible self-correction is intentional. Other endpoints: GET /v1/trace/{id} , GET /v1/evals/latest , GET /v1/defenses?days=7 , GET /v1/status , GET /v1/sources , GET /healthz .

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 14. Data model (Postgres)
chunks.text: Migrations with Alembic. Retention jobs as a nightly pg cron or app-level scheduler.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 15. Deployment
chunks.text: - VPS: one small always-on instance (e.g., Hetzner CX22-class: 2 vCPU, 4 GB). Never sleeps; no cold start for a recruiter's first question. - Compose: caddy , api , postgres (pgvector image), ingest (one-shot job image). Managed with Coolify or plain docker compose + systemd.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 15. Deployment
chunks.text: - Frontend: Cloudflare Pages. DNS and edge protection on Cloudflare. - CI/CD: GitHub Actions. On PR: lint, type check, unit tests, eval subset. On main: build image, push to GHCR, deploy via SSH pull, smoke test /healthz and one golden question, auto-rollback on fail.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 15. Deployment
chunks.text: - Secrets: OpenRouter key, Langfuse keys, Turnstile secret, canary, HMAC salt seed — env only, never in the repo, never in traces. - Backups: nightly pg dump to object storage, restore tested monthly. Corpus is also reproducible from the corpus repo. - Uptime: external check (e.g., UptimeRobot or Cloudflare health check) feeding /status .

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 16. Testing
chunks.text: Level What Unit Chunker, RRF fusion, answer-contract parser, claim id check, rate bucket math, budget transitions, redaction. Integration API + Postgres in docker: hybrid search returns expected ids on a fixture corpus; SSE event order; degraded mode at 100% budget; circuit breaker opens on mocked 429s.

chunks.title: zorzo.dev.br — backend spec
chunks.heading: zorzo.dev.br — Backend spec › 16. Testing
chunks.text: Contract Fake model server returning malformed JSON, fabricated source ids, canary leak — each must be caught by the right layer. Evals Section 11. Load 20 concurrent sessions on the VPS: p95 within target, rate limits hold. Model calls in unit/integration tests use a fake OpenRouter server.
